scope: PATH-01 batch affected-package display, plus R3-b read-only Python per-user package scope
status: implemented-and-isolated-ui-verified; real manager installation, real user base and real configuration write not performed
implementation: the batch preview dialog renders each writable tool's affected packages grouped under that tool, with name, version and an '入口可能失效' marker plus a per-tool unresolved count
a writable tool with no packages shows its note instead of an empty block, so an empty read is not silently omitted
commands::PythonUserScope reads the per-user install location read-only: PYTHONUSERBASE (process or user registry) with an APPDATA/Python fallback
a relative or unresolvable user base is reported as a reason rather than guessed
each versioned site-packages under the user base has its .dist-info/.egg-info entries counted; no Python process is executed
more than one versioned site-packages marks the location as shared by multiple interpreters
an unreadable versioned directory yields packages=None with the underlying error, never a fabricated zero
the uninstall preview's retained Python item now carries the resolved path, the distribution count and the shared-location warning
python_user_package_scope_at accepts a resolved base so fixtures never depend on the host environment

uiCoverage.batchPackages: packages-ui asserts 受影响的全局包, the eslint row marked as possibly unresolved, and the 2 个可能不再解析 total inside the batch dialog
uiCoverage.singlePackages: the previously added single-tool assertions still pass

notVerified: No real Python per-user installation was scanned; the user base was supplied from temporary fixtures
The shared-location flag is inferred from the number of versioned directories, not from interpreter registration
No real package-manager configuration was written; no packaging, tagging or release
limitations: The user-level package count covers .dist-info/.egg-info entries only; pipx venvs and external virtual environments are still listed as retained without enumeration
The uninstall preview reports a count, not the package names, for user-level packages
User-level packages remain non-removable by design; only the reporting changed
